OffOn Stream on FDA approves Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine Moderna was seeking approval for the vaccine's use in adults over 50. ByYouri Benadjaoud, Mary Kekatos, and Eric M. Strauss August 6, 2026, 3:59 AM Share The Food and Drug Administration approved Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine on Wednesday. The vaccine, mFLUSIVA, is expected to be available for people 50 and older for the 2026-2027 respiratory illness season. "Flu remains a significant public health challenge, and mFLUSIVA provides an important new option for America's seniors. This approval also reflects the ongoing potential of our mRNA platform to help address important public health challenges through continued scientific innovation," Stéphane Bancel, Chief Executive Officer of Moderna, said in a statement. In this Dec. 15, 2020, file photo, the Moderna, Inc. headquarters is shown in Cambridge, Mass. Elise Amendola/AP, FILE In a clinical trial for people aged 50 to 64, the mRNA vaccine led to 27% fewer confirmed flu cases than the current standard vaccine. The safety profile for Moderna’s vaccine and the current standard was about the same, but more people taking the mRNA vaccine reported side effects; those were mostly mild and lasted two days or less. For people 65 and older, a high-dose vaccine is currently recommended. Moderna said it will keep data this winter on how mFlusiva does compared to the current high-dose vaccine and submit that to the FDA to see if the vaccine remains approved for that population. Earlier this year, the FDA announced it would not review Moderna's application for the vaccine. However, the agency backtracked and agreed to review the shot after Moderna promised to conduct another study after the shot became available on the market. The Food and Drug Administration approved Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine on Wednesday. Kennedy Jr. has been vocal about his disapproval of the mRNA vaccine platform. Last year, the Department of Health and Human Services canceled at least $500 million of federally funded mRNA vaccine development. Kennedy also falsely claimed mRNA vaccines can prolong pandemics. Related Flu activity nationwide declines but ER visits for school-aged kids increasing: CDC Vaccine specialists have emphasized that using the mRNA vaccine platform would help expedite production of shots and allow vaccines to better match currently circulating strains of viruses, because they can be produced quicker than the traditional way. The flu vaccine is currently recommended for everyone over the age of 6 months by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. It is typically recommended to receive the shot before the end of October. The vaccine helps reduce the risk of severe illness, including hospitalization and death. This is a developing story. analysis.time: The Food and Drug Administration approved Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine on Wednesday, August 6, 2026 (N4). The approval is for the 2026-2027 respiratory illness season, with the vaccine expected to be available for people 50 and older (N5).
analysis.location_and_population: The approval is relevant to the United States, specifically targeting individuals aged 50 and older (N5). The vaccine is part of the broader seasonal influenza prevention strategy, which includes recommendations for everyone over 6 months (N23).
analysis.event: The FDA approved Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine, mFLUSIVA, for use in adults over 50 (N2). This approval was initially delayed but was reconsidered after Moderna committed to additional studies (N15).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: In a clinical trial for people aged 50 to 64, the mRNA vaccine led to 27% fewer confirmed flu cases than the current standard vaccine (N10). The safety profile was similar to the standard vaccine, though more people reported mild side effects (N11). The vaccine is expected to reduce the risk of severe illness, including hospitalization and death (N25).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Moderna will continue to monitor the vaccine's performance this winter and submit data to the FDA to assess its effectiveness for older adults (N13). The approval is a developing story, with updates expected (N26).

analysis.brief_en: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine, mFLUSIVA, for use in adults over 50 on August 6, 2026 (N4). This approval was initially delayed but was reconsidered after Moderna promised additional studies (N15). The vaccine is expected to be available for the 2026-2027 respiratory season, targeting individuals aged 50 and older (N5). In a clinical trial involving people aged 50 to 64, mFLUSIVA reduced confirmed flu cases by 27% compared to the standard vaccine (N10). The safety profile was similar to the standard vaccine, though more people reported mild side effects (N11). The vaccine is designed to reduce the risk of severe illness, including hospitalization and death (N25). Moderna plans to monitor its performance this winter and submit data to the FDA to determine its continued approval for older adults (N13). The approval is part of a broader strategy to address seasonal influenza, with the CDC recommending flu vaccines for everyone over 6 months (N23).

This approval was initially delayed but was reconsidered after Moderna promised additional studies (N15). The vaccine is expected to be available for the 2026-2027 respiratory season, targeting individuals aged 50 and older (N5). In a clinical trial involving people aged 50 to 64, mFLUSIVA reduced confirmed flu cases by 27% compared to the standard vaccine (N10). The safety profile was similar to the standard vaccine, though more people reported mild side effects (N11). The vaccine is designed to reduce the risk of severe illness, including hospitalization and death (N25). Moderna plans to monitor its performance this winter and submit data to the FDA to determine its continued approval for older adults (N13). news.content_zh: 美国食品和药物管理局 (FDA) 于 2026 年 8 月 6 日 (N4) 批准 Moderna 的 mRNA 季节性流感 疫苗、mFLUSIVA 用于 50 岁以上成人。该批准最初被推迟,但在 Moderna 承诺进行更多研究后重新考虑(N15)。疫苗 预计将在 2026-2027 年呼吸季节上市,目标人群为 50 岁及以上 (N5) 人群。在一项涉及 50 至 64 岁人群的临床试验中,与标准 疫苗 (N10) 相比,mFLUSIVA 将流感确诊病例减少了 27%。安全性与标准 疫苗 相似,但更多人报告有轻微副作用 (N11)。疫苗 旨在降低严重疾病的风险,包括住院和死亡 (N25)。Moderna 计划在今年冬天监测其表现,并向 FDA 提交数据,以确定其继续批准用于老年人 (N13)。此次批准是解决 季节性流感 问题的更广泛战略的一部分,CDC 建议 6 个月以上 (N23) 的所有人使用流感 季节性流感。

N Ne.V. 22.10.2026. 09:35h Vaccination against seasonal influenza for the 2026/2027 season begins on October 26 and will be carried out in health centers throughout Montenegro, the Institute of Public Health of Montenegro (IJZCG) announced today. The statement added that citizens can find out about the place and method of vaccination at their health center. "Vaccination is recommended primarily for people who are at increased risk of developing more severe forms of influenza and complications: people over 65 years of age, people with chronic diseases regardless of age, pregnant women, healthcare workers, as well as people who live in collective accommodation or provide care to people at increased risk," the statement states. The Institute of Public Health of Montenegro added that the flu can cause serious health complications, especially in people with chronic diseases, the elderly and other members of sensitive groups. Protection develops over the following weeks after vaccination, so it is recommended to receive the vaccine in a timely manner, in accordance with the advice of a healthcare professional," the statement reads. The Institute of Public Health of Montenegro said that in addition to vaccination, it is important to apply general protection measures against influenza and other respiratory infections: wash your hands regularly, ventilate rooms, avoid close contact with people who have symptoms of infection and, when necessary, wear a mask in enclosed spaces. "People with symptoms of respiratory infection should stay at home and contact their chosen doctor for advice. If they must stay in common areas, wearing a mask is recommended to reduce the risk of transmission of infection, especially to people from sensitive groups," the Institute of Public Health of Montenegro said. The institution said that they regularly monitor the movement of influenza and other acute respiratory infections and that they cooperate with health institutions in order to monitor and respond to the epidemiological situation in a timely manner. "Current information and recommendations regarding the flu are available on the website of the Institute of Public Health of Montenegro: www.ijzcg.me/grip," the IJZCG statement reads. The Institute of Public Health of Montenegro announced yesterday that the laboratory of the Center for Medical Microbiology of the Institute of Public Health of Montenegro, using the PCR diagnostic method, confirmed the first two cases of influenza virus infection in Montenegro in the 2026/2027 season. news.source_body_en: The Institute of Public Health of Montenegro (IJZCG) announced the start of seasonal flu vaccination for the 2026/2027 season on October 26, 2026. The vaccination campaign is recommended primarily for high-risk groups, including individuals over 65 years of age, people with chronic diseases, pregnant women, healthcare workers, and those living in collective accommodations or providing care to vulnerable individuals. IJZCG emphasized that vaccination is the most effective measure to reduce the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death. The institution also highlighted the importance of general protective measures against influenza and other respiratory infections, such as regular handwashing, room ventilation, avoiding close contact with infected individuals, and wearing masks in enclosed spaces when necessary. Additionally, IJZCG stated that they regularly monitor the spread of influenza and collaborate with health institutions to respond to the epidemiological situation promptly. Citizens are encouraged to consult their local health centers for details on vaccination locations and methods.
news.content_zh: 黑山公共卫生研究所 (IJZCG) 宣布于 2026 年 10 月 26 日开始启动 2026/2027 年季节性流感 疫苗接种。疫苗接种 活动主要针对高危人群,包括 65 岁以上的个人、慢性病患者、孕妇、医护人员以及居住在集体住宿或为弱势群体提供护理的人员。IJZCG强调,疫苗接种是降低重症、住院和死亡风险的最有效措施。该机构还强调了针对流感和其他呼吸道感染的一般防护措施的重要性,例如定期洗手、室内通风、避免与感染者密切接触以及必要时在封闭空间内佩戴​​口罩。此外,IJZCG表示,他们定期监测流感传播情况,并与卫生机构合作,及时应对流行病学情况。鼓励公民咨询当地卫生中心,了解有关 疫苗接种 地点和方法的详细信息。

Key Takeaways 2026–2027 flu vaccines are updated to better match the influenza viruses expected to circulate this season, including an updated H3N2 component. September and October are generally good times to get a flu shot. Vaccination can still provide protection later in the flu season. At-home flu tests can help you decide what to do next, but a negative test does not rule out the flu. Flu antiviral medications work best when started within the first 1–2 days of symptoms. Flu season is almost upon us. You may be wondering when to get a flu vaccine, whether at-home flu tests can help, and what to know about the influenza viruses expected to circulate this season. What’s actually different this year, and what should you do if you or your family gets sick? University of Rochester Medicine Infectious Disease expert Angela Branche, MD, breaks down what has changed for the 2026-2027 flu season, options for testing and treatment, and why vaccination remains important. What’s Different About the 2026–2027 Flu Season? For the 2026–2027 season, all three components of the U.S. flu vaccine have been updated from the previous season. The vaccine includes updated strains designed to protect against influenza viruses that are expected to circulate this season. One of the changes addresses influenza A(H3N2) viruses, including the subclade K viruses that circulated widely last year. It is too early to know exactly how severe the 2026–2027 flu season will be or which viruses will dominate. Flu activity can vary from year to year and from one community to another. See a Doctor at Home University of Rochester Medicine Virtual Urgent Care clinicians can use home test results to help guide next steps, lowering the risk of further exposure that can come with in-person urgent care. Get Care Now What’s the Difference Between Flu A and Flu B? There are two main types of seasonal influenza viruses that infect people: influenza A and influenza B. Influenza A is the type most often responsible for large outbreaks and severe seasons. It mutates more frequently and includes subtypes like H3N2. Influenza B usually circulates later in the season and tends to cause milder illness overall, though it can still be serious. What Are the Symptoms of Flu? Symptoms can vary, but common flu symptoms include: Fever and chills Muscle and body aches Severe fatigue Nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea (especially in children) Cough or shortness of breath Flu symptoms can overlap with other respiratory illnesses, including COVID-19 and RSV. Taking a flu test or talking with a health care provider can help determine the next step. What to Do If You Think You Have the Flu If you start feeling sick, it's important to get tested early. Flu antiviral medications, like Tamiflu, work best when started within the first 1-2 days of developing symptoms. Are At-Home Flu Tests Accurate? “At-home flu tests are about 70 to 80 percent accurate,” says Dr. Branche. “But a negative test doesn’t rule out the flu.” If your test is negative but your symptoms are severe or worsening, it’s essential to contact your healthcare provider or visit an urgent care facility. University of Rochester Medicine Virtual Urgent Care clinicians can use home test results to help guide next steps, lowering the risk of further exposure that can come with in-person urgent care. Have a positive flu test? Start a video visit now When Should I Seek Care for the Flu? Antiviral medications like oseltamivir (Tamiflu) work best when started early. Within the first 48 hours of symptoms, antiviral treatment can shorten illness and reduce severity for most people. High-risk patients—including pregnant people, older adults, those with chronic heart or lung disease, or weakened immune systems—should seek care even if symptoms started more than two days ago. Seek urgent care right away if you have: Trouble breathing or chest pain Persistent high fever Severe dehydration from vomiting or diarrhea Confusion or sudden dizziness Can You Have the Flu and COVID-19 at the Same Time? Yes, but it isn't common. Because flu, COVID-19, and RSV can cause similar symptoms, testing can help determine what's causing your illness. Flu Vaccines and Protection Flu vaccination is recommended every year for most people 6 months and older. The 2026–2027 flu vaccine has been updated to better match influenza viruses expected to circulate this season. “The flu vaccine may not prevent you from getting infected this year,” Branche says, “but it can still reduce your risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and complications.” Vaccines help the immune system build memory, working alongside protection from past infections. Even partial immunity can make symptoms milder and recovery faster. When Should I Get a Flu Shot? For most people who need one dose of the flu vaccine, September and October are generally the best times to get vaccinated. Ideally, you should get your flu shot by the end of October, but vaccination can still provide protection later in the flu season. Flu vaccines are safe, widely available, and can still provide meaningful protection throughout the season. A nasal spray flu vaccine is available for some healthy people ages 2 through 49. Ask your health care provider whether it's appropriate for you. It takes about two weeks for your body to build its immune response after vaccination. Can the Flu Vaccine Give You the Flu? No. The flu vaccine cannot give you influenza. Some people have mild side effects after vaccination, such as soreness, fatigue, or a low-grade fever. Can You Get Flu, COVID-19, and RSV Vaccines at the Same Time? You may be able to get more than one vaccine at the same time. Talk with your doctor to determine which vaccines you need and when to get them. Protecting Babies from RSV Infants can be protected from severe RSV through either vaccination during pregnancy or an RSV antibody given to the baby. Talk with your pediatrician or prenatal care provider about which option is best for your baby. Why Does Vaccine Research Matter? Influenza viruses change constantly, which is why flu vaccines are updated every year. Vaccines use a piece of the virus to train the immune system. Unfortunately, that same part of the virus mutates easily. Researchers at University of Rochester Medicine and around the world are working to improve vaccine technology, including studies exploring broader and longer-lasting protection. “It’s a constant battle of humans against viruses, and sometimes we win, and sometimes we don’t,” explains Branche. “That’s why developing new vaccine technologies is so important. There’s always a way to do better.” Cold, Flu, and RSV Guide As we move into winter, illnesses like flu, RSV, COVID-19, and stomach bugs become more common. Stay updated on flu, RSV, and other seasonal illnesses: symptoms, prevention tips, and when to seek care. Get the latest info Connect with us! analysis.time: The 2026–2027 flu season is approaching, with vaccination recommended in September and October (N2, N4, N47).
analysis.location_and_population: The article is published by the University of Rochester Medicine, focusing on the U.S. population (N2, N13).
analysis.event: The 2026–2027 flu vaccine has been updated to better match the influenza viruses expected to circulate this season, including an updated H3N2 component (N3, N13, N14, N43).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The severity of the flu season and dominant viruses are not yet known, but the vaccine includes updated strains to protect against expected circulating viruses (N17, N15).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Vaccination is recommended for most people 6 months and older, and at-home flu tests can help guide next steps, though they are not 100% accurate (N24, N31, N32, N39, N42).

analysis.brief_en: The University of Rochester Medicine has published information about the upcoming 2026–2027 flu season, emphasizing the importance of vaccination and testing. The flu vaccine for this season has been updated to better match the influenza viruses expected to circulate, including an updated H3N2 component. Vaccination is recommended for most individuals aged 6 months and older, with September and October identified as the optimal months for getting a flu shot. At-home flu tests are available but have an accuracy rate of 70 to 80 percent, and a negative result does not rule out the flu. The article also highlights the differences between influenza A and B, noting that A is more likely to cause severe outbreaks. While the severity of the flu season and dominant viruses are not yet known, the vaccine aims to reduce the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and complications. The article advises seeking urgent care for severe symptoms and mentions that antiviral medications like Tamiflu are most effective when started within the first 1–2 days of symptoms. It also notes that flu can occur alongside other respiratory illnesses such as COVID-19 and RSV, making testing essential for accurate diagnosis.

At Hà Nội Children's Hospital, flu patients currently account for about half of pediatric inpatients in its infectious disease department. Children with influenza A being cared at Thanh Nhàn Hospital in Hà Nội in mid-October. — VNA/VNS Photo Lê Đông HÀ NỘI — The number of seasonal flu cases is on the rise in several localities, particularly among young children, while doctors have warned that the illness can cause serious complications despite most patients recovering within about a week. In the northern region, cases of influenza A among children have risen in recent weeks. The National Children's Hospital has received about 70 children with influenza A each week since early October, three times the number recorded in previous weeks, Tuổi Trẻ (Youth) newspaper reported. Most of the patients were under five years old, with some developing complications including pneumonia and respiratory failure. At Hà Nội Children's Hospital, flu patients currently account for about half of pediatric inpatients in its infectious disease department. The number of children seeking medical care for flu has increased since late August, with about 100 children visiting the hospital each day, of whom 10-20 per cent require hospitalisation. In HCM City, disease surveillance has also recorded a rise in acute respiratory infections. During the first week of October, the city recorded 151 flu cases, bringing the total since the beginning of the year to 397, with influenza A/H1N1 2009 accounting for the majority. Dr Đỗ Thiện Hải, deputy director of the National Children's Hospital's Centre for Tropical Diseases, said flu is common among children and cases may increase during seasonal transitions. Children under five are particularly susceptible, partly because they often spend time in schools and daycare centres, where viruses can spread easily, Hải said. Flu and the common cold share some symptoms, but there are differences. Children with flu typically develop a sudden high fever lasting about three days, accompanied by respiratory symptoms such as coughing, sneezing and a runny nose. Common colds generally cause milder symptoms and patients tend to recover more quickly, he said. Dr Lê Văn Chương, deputy head of the Infectious Diseases Department at Thủ Đức City Hospital in HCM City, warned that seasonal flu is not simply a common cold and can cause serious complications, particularly among high-risk groups. Older people, pregnant women, children and those with chronic conditions such as cardiovascular, respiratory or kidney diseases, anemia, metabolic disorders or weakened immune systems face a higher risk of severe illness, Chương said. People with underlying respiratory or cardiovascular conditions are particularly vulnerable to adverse outcomes from flu, while those taking immunosuppressive drugs or undergoing cancer treatment may develop more severe illness and require longer treatment, Hải said. Complications can include pneumonia and respiratory failure, while high fever may cause seizures in children. Although most patients recover within about a week, people should seek medical attention if symptoms persist or become unusual. Patients with persistent high fever, poor response to fever-reducing medication, severe fatigue or poor appetite should be taken to a medical facility for evaluation and timely treatment, doctors advised. No self-medication Doctors also warned against the self-directed use of antiviral drugs and antibiotics to treat flu at home. Antiviral drugs can shorten the duration of illness and reduce the risk of complications in some cases, particularly when treatment begins early, usually within 48 hours of symptom onset, Dr Chương said. Such drugs should be used under medical guidance rather than purchased and taken without consultation, he said. Antibiotics do not kill flu viruses and therefore should not routinely be used to treat influenza. Doctors may prescribe them when medically indicated, such as when a bacterial infection occurs alongside the flu. Doctors also recommended that families take preventive measures for children and older people, with annual flu vaccination being an important way to reduce the risk of infection and severe illness. — VNS Tags close Advertisements zodiac new ranking producer (EN)-20261026-14:18 arrow_forward_ios Read more CANCEL NEXT VIDEO play_arrow volume_mute AD PausePlay % buffered00:00 00:03 00:36 UnmuteMute Play E-paper E-paper Subscribe Print Advertisement Online Advertisement Latest Most read HKSTP Partners with Leading Science and Technology Company Merck to Open a New Chapter in I&T Collaboration 1. analysis.time: October 21, 2026 (publication date), with flu cases rising since late August and increasing in recent weeks.
analysis.location_and_population: Hà Nội and Ho Chi Minh City, particularly affecting children under five years old and individuals with chronic conditions.
analysis.event: Doctors have warned of serious complications from seasonal flu, including pneumonia, respiratory failure, and seizures in children, while noting that most patients recover within a week. The National Children's Hospital reported a significant increase in influenza A cases, with about 70 children admitted weekly since early October.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The number of children seeking medical care for flu has increased since late August, with about 100 children visiting hospitals daily. analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Doctors advised seeking medical attention for persistent symptoms, using antiviral drugs under medical guidance, and avoiding routine use of antibiotics. analysis.brief_en: Doctors in Vietnam have issued warnings about the serious complications associated with seasonal flu, particularly among children and high-risk groups. The National Children's Hospital in Hà Nội reported a significant rise in influenza A cases, with about 70 children admitted weekly since early October, three times the number from previous weeks. In Ho Chi Minh City, acute respiratory infections have also increased. Most patients recover within a week, but complications such as pneumonia, respiratory failure, and seizures in children can occur. Medical professionals emphasized the importance of timely treatment, using antiviral drugs under guidance, and avoiding unnecessary antibiotic use. They also recommended annual flu vaccination as a key preventive measure. The situation is being closely monitored, with concerns raised about the potential severity of the illness in vulnerable populations.

In the first four days of vaccination alone, around 600 people have been vaccinated at the Pristina Family Medicine Center, with the greatest interest being among the elderly and people with chronic diseases. Just four days after the start of seasonal flu vaccination, around 600 citizens have been vaccinated at the Main Family Medicine Center in Pristina. Breathe Cleaner Air Discover 7 simple ways to make your indoor air fresh and pure. familyhandyman.com > Gani Zabeli, a resident of the Kalabria neighborhood in Pristina, says that he gets the flu vaccine every year. Breathe Cleaner Air Discover 7 simple ways to make your indoor air fresh and pure. familyhandyman.com > "For more than 15 years, every fall I have been getting this vaccine to protect myself from these winter diseases, which are mainly inflammations, viruses, and so on. Since these are free, the state provides them and we have an excellent service. I didn't wait a minute or two and got the vaccine here. Why not get it to gain immunity in our body," said Zabeli. And the doctor at the Main Center for Family Medicine, Rineta Turku, says that the greatest interest in vaccination is among the elderly and those suffering from chronic diseases. "The seasonal flu vaccination process has started on Monday, October 22. Citizens can perform this service at the Main Family Medicine Center and in 15 other Family Medicine centers, where there are vaccination units. Citizens' interest is extremely good. People with chronic diseases and the elderly are most interested," said Turku. Seasonal flu vaccines have arrived in Kosovo three weeks late. They were scheduled to arrive at the end of September, so that vaccination could begin in early October. analysis.event: Seasonal flu vaccination campaign started in Kosovo, with 600 citizens vaccinated in the first four days, primarily among the elderly and those with chronic diseases. The campaign was delayed by three weeks.

analysis.brief_en: A vaccination campaign against seasonal flu has begun in Kosovo, with 600 citizens receiving the vaccine in the first four days at the Main Family Medicine Center in Pristina and 15 other centers. The elderly and individuals with chronic diseases have shown the highest interest in getting vaccinated. The campaign was delayed by three weeks, as vaccines were scheduled to arrive by the end of September but arrived later. Seasonal influenza is an acute respiratory infection that spreads easily through droplets and can lead to serious complications, particularly in vulnerable groups such as the elderly and those with chronic illnesses. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends annual vaccination to reduce the risk of severe flu and health complications, along with hygiene measures like regular hand washing and covering the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing. The state provides free vaccines, and the service is described as excellent. No confirmed cases or deaths are reported in the supplied evidence.

news.content: English Login Homepage Topic News Political System Destination Event Travel Happy Vietnam Enterprise Product Heritage Museum Figure Multimedia Data Home Culture – Society Medical Seasonal influenza can cause serious complications in humans; the Ministry of Health recommends 8 preventive measures. Seasonal influenza is primarily transmitted from person to person through respiratory droplets containing the virus, which are released when an infected person coughs, sneezes, or talks. The risk of infection is especially high with close contact with an infected person, in crowded places, or in enclosed, poorly ventilated spaces. Báo Đại biểu Nhân dân•21/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 According to the Department of Disease Prevention, Ministry of Health , seasonal influenza is an acute infectious disease caused by the influenza virus, circulating year-round in Vietnam. The number of cases may increase at certain times of the year, depending on the region and weather conditions, especially during transitional seasons and the cold months of autumn and winter. The disease is primarily transmitted from person to person through respiratory droplets containing the virus, which are spread when an infected person coughs, sneezes, or talks. The risk of infection increases with close contact with an infected person, in crowded places, or in enclosed, poorly ventilated spaces. Most people with the flu experience mild symptoms and recover on their own. However, the disease can still become severe and cause complications, especially in high-risk groups such as people over 65, children under 5, pregnant women, women who have given birth within the last two weeks, and people with underlying health conditions. Khám phá thêm Tìm hiểu lịch sử Đọc Mẹo Du Lịch Khám phá ĐNA Underlying conditions that increase the risk of severe complications include cardiovascular disease, chronic lung disease, kidney failure, cirrhosis, diabetes, and immunodeficiency. Therefore, proactive prevention, symptom recognition, and health monitoring are crucial in limiting the risk of infection and complications. Underlying conditions that increase the risk of developing severe seasonal influenza include cardiovascular disease, chronic lung disease, kidney failure, cirrhosis, diabetes, and immunodeficiency. Seasonal influenza can cause serious complications, so the Ministry of Health recommends that people take the following 8 preventive measures: You may also like - Wear a mask correctly when visiting healthcare facilities, using public transportation, going to crowded places, or enclosed spaces with poor ventilation. - Cover your mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing with a disposable tissue or your elbow. Dispose of used tissues properly, and wash your hands immediately afterward. - Maintain personal hygiene, wash hands frequently with soap and clean water or hand sanitizer; avoid touching your eyes, nose, and mouth. - Limit close contact with people who have or are suspected of having respiratory illnesses. - Maintain a healthy lifestyle, exercise regularly, eat a balanced diet, get enough sleep, and keep your body warm to boost your immune system. - Individuals experiencing symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, and runny nose should limit contact with others, rest, monitor their health, and wear a mask when interacting with others. Patients should not self-medicate with antiviral or antibiotic drugs without a prescription from a healthcare professional. You may also like - Regularly clean and sanitize frequently touched surfaces; ensure living spaces, workplaces, and classrooms are well-ventilated, and improve ventilation in enclosed areas. - Individuals at high risk of developing severe symptoms from the flu should limit their exposure to crowded places. If symptoms appear, they should proactively contact or visit a healthcare facility for timely advice, examination, and treatment. At the same time, the Department of Disease Prevention will continue to coordinate with relevant units to monitor the developments of seasonal influenza, update information, provide professional guidance, and implement appropriate prevention and control measures. The 2026-2027 flu season appears to be off to an early and strong start, experts say. Influenza activity is still low nationally, but cases are rising quickly in many parts of the country, especially the West, and two states, Louisiana and Hawaii, are already reporting moderate levels. As of Oct. 21, flu infections are growing or likely growing in 44 states, according to the latest estimates from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. That’s not surprising, given that flu activity typically ticks up around this time of year. However, this year’s flu season started way ahead of schedule, with infections rising as early as August. “Early-season influenza activity is currently higher than typically observed at this time of year,” the CDC said in its FluView surveillance report for the week ending Oct. 17. Influenza A H1N1 is fueling the vast majority of cases in the U.S. so far this season, per CDC data. That’s a shift from last winter, when H3N2 subclade K — aka, the “superflu” — was the dominant strain. What’s more, it appears that the H1N1 strain circulating has picked up a new mutation which may affect its ability to evade pre-existing immunity. If H1N1 sounds familiar, that’s because it’s the infamous “swine flu” strain that caused a pandemic in 2009. As the mutated H1N1 strain spreads, doctors are urging people to get the 2026-2027 flu vaccine. Why Is Flu Season Starting So Early? No two flu seasons look the same because the timing and severity can vary from year to year. It’s still too early to tell if this flu season will end up being more severe or what role the mutated H1N1 strain might play, the CDC tells TODAY.com in a statement. However, there are multiple indicators that flu activity is higher than usual for this time of year. Cases started increasing in late August and early September and have been rising steadily since, per the CDC. The percent of flu tests coming back positive was 5.7% during the week ending Oct. 17. Last year during the same time period, the weekly test positivity rate was less than 1%, per the CDC National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System dashboard. Outpatient visits to doctor’s offices or urgent cares for flu-like illness hit 2.2% during the week ending Oct. 17, which is higher than the previous two seasons, CDC data show. Hospitalizations and deaths from the flu are also rising. “Cases are still relatively low, so we’re still in the early phases of a flu surge,” Andrew Pekosz, Ph.D., a virologist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, tells TODAY.com. It’s unclear why exactly cases are rising earlier than normal. One potential reason is that people may have less pre-existing immunity to the H1N1 strain with a new mutation. “Maybe that’s why people are getting sick sooner,” Dr. Bernard Camins, an infectious disease physician and professor at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, tells TODAY.com. The H1N1 strain spreading is different from the H3N2 strain that dominated last winter. “Even people who got the flu last year are vulnerable,” says Camins. When H1N1 started ramping up in late August, the updated flu shots had just started rolling out. “The pattern we oftentimes see with early season flu is that the first strain that gets here is the one that escapes immunity the most,” Pekosz adds. Does an early flu season mean a more severe flu season? Not necessarily, experts say. It’s too early to tell how the 2026-2027 flu season will pan out, or whether it’ll be milder compared to last year’s. The U.S. saw a harsh flu season last winter fueled by the highly mutated H3N2 subclade K variant, aka the “super flu.” “We still have to see how bad it will be this year, but I think it is just starting earlier,” says Camins. “The only thing predictable about the flu is that it’s unpredictable,” Dr. Natalie Azar, NBC News medical contributor, said on TODAY. What Is the Mutated H1N1 Strain? Influenza viruses mutate constantly, which is why we get an updated flu shot every year. Last summer, H3N2 picked up a host of mutations, which led to the emergence the subclade K variant. H1N1 viruses typically change less often than H3N2 viruses, the CDC says. However, this year, H1N1 (pdm09), subclade D.3.1.1, acquired one new mutation, G155E, says Pekosz. Recommended Gift Guides Gift GuidesHold Off the Socks — We Have Editor-Picked Gifts for Young Men Gift Guides Gift GuidesThe Best and Most Useful Gifts for 21-Year-Olds The mutation was first identified in September in Seattle, Washington, according in a preprint paper published to bioRxiv. “It is different from last year’s H1N1 virus, and that mutation position (G155E) we know is important for generating protective antibody responses,” Pekosz explains. This means the H1N1 strain may be better able to escape immunity because the antibodies people have from previous infection or vaccination may not recognize it as well. “How that (mutation) is going to affect the disease spread and severity is not clear,” says Pekosz. Even if the H1N1 strain circulating does not match the one included in the 2026-2027 flu vaccines, the shot is still expected to provide protection. “A mismatch is not a black-or-white situation. We may have less immunity, not no immunity,” Pekosz adds. Historically, H1N1 has hit young people particularly hard. The new mutation may make children more susceptible, especially if they haven’t been exposed to H1N1 yet, Azar said. “It is too early to know what viruses may predominate or to say whether there might be implications on flu vaccine effectiveness this season,” the CDC said in its latest FluView report. H1N1 Flu Symptoms The flu often hits suddenly and intensely, says Camins. Common symptoms of the flu include: Fever Chills Fatigue Body aches Runny nose Coughing It can be difficult to distinguish the signs of a flu infection from those caused by COVID, which is why testing is important, Camins says. If you test positive for influenza, you can seek treatment with antivirals, which can lessen symptom severity and duration. Antivirals are an especially important tool for high-risk groups, including people over the age of 65, children under the age of 5, and immunocompromised individuals. These medications aren’t available over-the-counter, so you’ll need to see a doctor first. “You have to get that prescription fast ... within the first 48 hours after symptom onset, (or else) they don’t work as well,” says Pekosz. If you experience severe flu symptoms, contact your doctor. When to Get the Flu Shot There’s no reason to panic over the mutated H1N1 strain, the experts emphasize, but it is a good reminder to protect yourself. “View (this) as a a sign to go out and get the flu vaccine,” says Pekosz. Getting a flu shot is the most effective way to prevent against severe illness, complications and death from the flu. The 2026-2027 flu vaccines are available at most pharmacies, doctors’ offices and clinics. The updated shots protect against three viruses: influenza A H1N1 (pdm09), influenza A H3N2 and influenza B. There are multiple options available, including standard flu shots, high-dose shots, a nasal mist and the new mRNA flu vaccine. “Even if there’s a mismatched strain, there’s two other strains that the vaccine will provide better protection against,” says Pekosz. Different flu strains can circulate later in the season, so the shot can protect you throughout the winter and early spring. The flu shot is never 100% effective, Camins adds, and you can still get infected if you’ve been vaccinated — but you won’t get nearly as sick or end up in the hospital. Vaccination is especially important if you’re considered high-risk, but everyone can benefit. The best time to get the flu shot is before the end of October, but you can still benefit if you get it later, the experts note. “If you haven’t gotten it yet for whatever reason, now’s the time to get vaccinated because the flu season is starting a little bit sooner and you need at least two weeks for the vaccine immunity to (reach) protective levels,” Pekosz adds. If you aren’t sure which flu vaccine you should get, talk to your doctor or pharmacist. Newsletter Videos Podcasts Contact Us Our Office General Enquiries Media Enquiries NMC Enquiries Disease Index Search Close End of the 2026 influenza season 21 October , 2026 The 2026 influenza season ended in week 39 (week ending 27 September 2026). In South Africa, the influenza season typically begins around mid-to-late April and ends around late August to mid-September. The 2026 season began in week 11 (week starting 9 March 2026), when the influenza detection rate among patients enrolled in inpatient pneumonia surveillance at public hospitals exceeded the seasonal threshold and remained above it for two consecutive weeks. This was earlier than most previous seasons but similar to 2025, when the season started in week 13 (week starting 24 March 2025). Influenza activity subsequently increased and peaked in week 20 (week starting 11 May 2026). The detection rate subsequently dropped below the seasonal threshold from week 40 (week starting 28 September 2026) and remained below the threshold for two consecutive weeks. From 29 December 2025 to 11 October 2026 across the three sentinel surveillance systems (outpatient influenza-like-illness (ILI) surveillance at public primary health care clinics, outpatient ILI surveillance at private general practitioner practices, and inpatient pneumonia surveillance at public hospitals), influenza was detected in 1029 of 6212 specimens tested (16.6%) . Among the cases for which a subtype could be determined (97.1%; 999/1029), 44.0% (453/1029) were influenza A(H3N2), 32.6% (335/1029) were influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 and 20.5% (211/1029) were influenza B (211/1029; 20.5%). Additionally, seven dual infections were detected: one case of A(H1N1) and A(H3N2), one case of A(H3N2) and influenza B, two cases of A(H1N1) and influenza B, and three cases of an inconclusive influenza A subtype and influenza B. Before routine lineage subtyping of influenza B was discontinued in June 2026, 100% (111/111) of tested influenza B samples were B/Victoria. Message to clinicians Influenza is an acute respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses. It spreads easily between people through respiratory droplets and causes seasonal epidemics. Most people recover without treatment, but influenza can cause severe illness or death, especially in people at high risk of severe influenza illness or complications. Although the 2026 influenza season has ended, sporadic influenza infections may continue to occur outside the defined seasonal period. Clinicians should therefore continue to consider influenza in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with respiratory illness and in patients with highly suggestive symptoms. High-risk groups include pregnant women, individuals living with HIV, those with chronic conditions such as diabetes, lung disease, tuberculosis, heart disease, renal disease, and obesity, older individuals (≥65 years), and children under two years old. Where to find updated data Weekly reports documenting respiratory pathogen circulation in South Africa, including influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Bordetella pertussis, human adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, human parainfluenza virus and human rhinovirus, are available on the NICD website here. Statements Blogs Newsletter Videos Podcasts Contact Us Our Office General Enquiries Media Enquiries NMC Enquiries Disease Index Search Close End of the 2026 influenza season 21 October , 2026 The 2026 influenza season ended in week 39 (week ending 27 September 2026). In South Africa, the influenza season typically begins around mid-to-late April and ends around late August to mid-September. The 2026 season began in week 11 (week starting 9 March 2026), when the influenza detection rate among patients enrolled in inpatient pneumonia surveillance at public hospitals exceeded the seasonal threshold and remained above it for two consecutive weeks. This was earlier than most previous seasons but similar to 2025, when the season started in week 13 (week starting 24 March 2025). Influenza activity subsequently increased and peaked in week 20 (week starting 11 May 2026). The detection rate subsequently dropped below the seasonal threshold from week 40 (week starting 28 September 2026) and remained below the threshold for two consecutive weeks. From 29 December 2025 to 11 October 2026 across the three sentinel surveillance systems (outpatient influenza-like-illness (ILI) surveillance at public primary health care clinics, outpatient ILI surveillance at private general practitioner practices, and inpatient pneumonia surveillance at public hospitals), influenza was detected in 1029 of 6212 specimens tested (16.6%) . Among the cases for which a subtype could be determined (97.1%; 999/1029), 44.0% (453/1029) were influenza A(H3N2), 32.6% (335/1029) were influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 and 20.5% (211/1029) were influenza B (211/1029; 20.5%). Additionally, seven dual infections were detected: one case of A(H1N1) and A(H3N2), one case of A(H3N2) and influenza B, two cases of A(H1N1) and influenza B, and three cases of an inconclusive influenza A subtype and influenza B. Before routine lineage subtyping of influenza B was discontinued in June 2026, 100% (111/111) of tested influenza B samples were B/Victoria. Message to clinicians Influenza is an acute respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses. It spreads easily between people through respiratory droplets and causes seasonal epidemics. Most people recover without treatment, but influenza can cause severe illness or death, especially in people at high risk of severe influenza illness or complications. Although the 2026 influenza season has ended, sporadic influenza infections may continue to occur outside the defined seasonal period. Clinicians should therefore continue to consider influenza in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with respiratory illness and in patients with highly suggestive symptoms. High-risk groups include pregnant women, individuals living with HIV, those with chronic conditions such as diabetes, lung disease, tuberculosis, heart disease, renal disease, and obesity, older individuals (≥65 years), and children under two years old. Where to find updated data Weekly reports documenting respiratory pathogen circulation in South Africa, including influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Bordetella pertussis, human adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, human parainfluenza virus and human rhinovirus, are available on the NICD website here. news.content: INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS TIMES uk Newsletter My account Log Out Oct 26, 11:04 PM GMT World UK News Markets Business SME Personal Finance Tech Entertainment Lifestyle Reviews Newsletter My account Log Out UK Edition World UK News Markets Business - Retail - Hospitality - Healthcare - Electrification of Auto - Finance & Banking - Cybersecurity - Artificial Intelligence - New Cities - Education - esport - Healthcare SME Personal Finance Tech Entertainment Lifestyle Reviews Listings & More Newsletter Fintech Shopping and Sponsored Latest News Most Popular News Trending Sports Industry Reports Editions Australia Edition India Edition Singapore Edition United Kingdom United States Newsletter Follow Us Editions Australia Edition India Edition Singapore Edition United Kingdom United States World Early US Flu Season Surges as Mutated H1N1 Raises Vaccine Concerns The West Coast has the most activity, but CDC says national levels are still low and there's no evidence that G155E causes more severe illness By Ma. Patrice Anne A. Martin Published 24 October 2026, 6:50 AM BST Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share on Reddit Share on Flipboard Share on Pocket US flu activity rises early as mutated H1N1 raises questions about vaccine protection Polina Tankilevitch/Pexels Flu activity in the US is climbing earlier than usual, with the West Coast already seeing the highest levels by early October and the A(H1)pdm09 strain dominating national cases. Scientists are closely tracking an emerging G155E mutation in some H1N1 viruses that affects an antigenic region of the virus and may alter how antibodies recognise it, although overall activity across the country remains low. US flu activity began increasing in late August and September 2026, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). By the week ending 10 October, the West Coast, including HHS regions 9 and 10, was recording the highest activity. For the week ending 17 October, 2,918 of 51,490 respiratory specimens tested by clinical laboratories were positive for influenza, giving a positivity rate of 5.7 per cent. Influenza A accounted for 97.9 per cent of positive specimens. Although activity is increasing, national levels remain low overall. An early start does not necessarily mean a more severe flu season. H1N1 Dominates Early Flu Activity as G155E Spreads The CDC reported that 239 of 241 influenza A viruses subtyped by public health laboratories during the week ending 17 October were A(H1N1)pdm09, representing 99.2 per cent of those analysed. A(H1N1)pdm09 is an established influenza virus that emerged in 2009 and continues to circulate seasonally. Most A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses genetically characterised by the CDC this season belong to the D.3.1.1 subclade. Within this group, viruses carrying the G155E amino-acid substitution in the haemagglutinin protein have increased in recent weeks. The mutation occurs in an antigenic region of the virus and may affect how antibodies recognise some circulating viruses. The World Health Organization (WHO) reported in October that viruses carrying G155E had increased in recent weeks. Human-serum studies cited by WHO found reduced antibody responses to some recently circulating D.3.1.1 viruses carrying G155E and other substitutions, raising questions about how effectively existing antibodies recognise some circulating variants. However, the CDC's separate antigenic testing found that 82 of 88 characterised H1N1 viruses were well recognised by ferret antisera to the vaccine reference virus. This laboratory finding does not establish how effectively vaccination protects people against circulating variants in real-world conditions. The CDC says it is too early to determine the impact of these genetic changes on vaccine effectiveness. There is also insufficient evidence that G155E caused the early rise in flu activity or makes the virus more severe. Read more What Is Shamonda Virus? Cause, Symptoms and Vaccine Questions After First Human Case in France Ends in Death WHO Chief Confirms First Human Shamonda Virus Infection After Patient Dies in France Shamonda Virus Found in Human for First Time After Decades of Being Considered Non-Transmissible PA Measles Outbreak Hits 1,286 Cases; 66 Pregnant Women Infected, at Least Six Babies Born With the Virus Experts Call For Vaccination as Monitoring Continues The CDC recommends annual flu vaccination for everyone aged six months and older, unless they have a relevant contraindication. Vaccination can reduce the risk of serious complications, hospitalisation and death, even though it does not prevent every infection. Young children, adults aged 65 and older, pregnant people and those with certain underlying health conditions face a higher risk of severe flu complications. The CDC also recommends handwashing, covering coughs and sneezes, and staying home when sick. People at higher risk who develop flu symptoms should seek medical advice promptly, as antiviral treatment can be most beneficial when started early. Early Flu Surge Sparks Debate Over Vaccination on Social Media The early rise in flu activity has prompted debate on social media, with users sharing personal experiences and questioning the effectiveness of flu vaccines. Scientists are closely tracking an emerging G155E mutation in some H1N1 viruses that affects an antigenic region of the virus and may alter how antibodies recognise it, although overall activity across the country remains low. US flu activity began increasing in late August and September 2026, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). By the week ending 10 October, the West Coast, including HHS regions 9 and 10, was recording the highest activity. For the week ending 17 October, 2,918 of 51,490 respiratory specimens tested by clinical laboratories were positive for influenza, giving a positivity rate of 5.7 per cent. Influenza A accounted for 97.9 per cent of positive specimens. Although activity is increasing, national levels remain low overall. An early start does not necessarily mean a more severe flu season. By Don Rauf Published on October 23, 2026 Fact-Checked by Emily Kay Votruba Add us on Google Flu season has arrived early this year, with a new variant of the virus already sickening thousands and sending many to the hospital. Usually in the United States, flu season begins in October, but this year cases began to rise starting in late August, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). [1] [2] Early data from the Walgreens 2026–27 Flu Index shows national flu activity tracking about four weeks ahead of expectations. [3] “By late September, test positivity was about eight times higher than at the same point last year,” says Ryan Maves, MD, a professor specializing in infectious disease at Wake Forest School of Medicine in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. Flu Numbers Are Up, and in Unexpected Places Although the CDC currently classifies overall flu activity as “low,” the national percentage of positive tests for influenza has climbed from 1.3 percent in early September to nearly 6 percent in mid-October. [1] The latest CDC surveillance data show that flu hospitalizations have more than doubled since a month ago, reaching more than 4,800 cases. “In addition to flu’s early arrival, the West Coast states are being hit first unexpectedly,” says Peter Chin-Hong, MD, an infectious-disease specialist and a professor of medicine at the University of California San Francisco School of Medicine. “Usually we see flu start off in the southern states, then move northeast, then westward across the country.” What Flu Strain Is Dominating Cases This Year? One of the forces driving the early surge in cases appears to be a new mutation in the predominant type of flu, influenza A (H1N1), which accounts for more than 96 percent of subtyped samples. [4] [5] Scientists have identified a genetic mutation, G155E, on the surface of the H1N1 protein that makes it harder for antibodies to recognize and block the virus from infecting human cells, according to Dr. Chin-Hong. “This change is making people who might have immunity carried over from last season, or vaccine immunity, not recognize the mutated flu quite as well,” he says. “It is likely more of an immune evasion advantage rather than a ‘super flu’ [associated with more severe symptoms]. There is no evidence so far that people are getting more seriously ill than usual,” adds Chin-Hong. A Mutation Detected Early in Japan May Explain Flu Rise in the West Several news sources have reported that G155E is likely causing a severe, early spike in flu in Japan. The mutation was identified there as early as May 2026, according to Northeastern Global News. [6] [7] To some degree, the flu wave in Japan connected to G155E may explain the increase in cases in the western United States, according to Thomas Russo, MD, an infectious-diseases expert at the Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences at SUNY Buffalo in New York. “Geographically, moving eastward from Japan, the western U.S. is the first stop,” says Dr. Russo. “In this era of international travel, this may in part explain the early rise in cases in the West.” California’s Department of Public Health is currently reporting “high” flu activity across most of the state, with the latest data indicating test positivity at nearly 10 percent. [8] In Hawaii, test positivity has reached a staggering 25.7 percent as of October 17. [9] Russo points out, however, that flu is gaining ground throughout the continental United States. “Here in Buffalo, we’re seeing more patients testing positive and landing in the hospital.” This Flu Season May Be Rough for Younger People Groups most at risk of severe illness due to flu, according to the CDC, include: [10] Adults age 65 and older Children younger than 2 years old People with weakened immune systems People who’ve had a stroke People with asthma, chronic lung disease, neurological conditions, heart disease, kidney disorders, liver disorders, and blood disorders People with severe obesity, or a body mass index of 40 or above Russo notes, however, that younger people may have less natural flu immunity and lower antibody neutralization against the circulating mutated H1N1 strain than many older adults. “In some tested serum [blood] samples from different demographic age groups, the ability for teens and people in their twenties to neutralize the virus was significantly less than in older people,” he says. “This makes sense because older people have seen a lot more influenza, so they’re more likely to develop prior antibodies that have some cross-protection, even though it’s a new variant.” Experts Say Get Your Flu Shot Now Based on past flu seasons and the latest virus trajectory, we can expect much more illness and hospitalizations in the weeks ahead, Russo says. “Flu season is well short of peak,” he says. Holiday gatherings will likely contribute to the spread, as people come together in closed spaces and air travel increases. With these factors in mind, public health authorities are urging the public to take measures now to protect themselves and others. The CDC advises getting a flu shot as soon as possible, as the annual seasonal flu vaccine is “the best way to help reduce the risk of getting flu and any of its potentially serious complications.” [11] Although the 2026–2027 flu shots were formulated before the G155E mutation emerged, the CDC still expects them to provide significant protection against severe illness this year. Research shows that during the 2022–23 flu season, many vaccinated people still got the flu, but the shot prevented about 70,000 hospitalizations. [12] In addition to vaccination, people may want to consider wearing a mask in crowded indoor environments, washing hands more often, and steering clear of others who are sick with flu, adds Dr. Maves. How Bad Will Flu Symptoms Be This Year? While flu season may have come early, there's no evidence so far that the illness itself will be more severe or that there will be any unique symptoms, according to Chin-Hong. No matter how harsh the virus proves to be, he urges the public to never underestimate the flu. “Every year influenza kills tens of thousands of Americans,” he says. “This is a virus that can cause serious pneumonia, worsening of heart and lung disease, brain disease in rare cases, and lead to hospitalizations and deaths, especially in vulnerable populations.” Most people get over the flu by taking care of themselves at home, but when physical signs become serious, you need to get immediate professional medical help. Chin-Hong says that severe symptoms that may require hospitalization include: Shortness of breath or trouble breathing Confusion Inability to keep down fluids For infants and very young children: Bluish lips or face, increased fussiness, and not urinating (fewer wet diapers) EDITORIAL SOURCES Everyday Health follows strict sourcing guidelines to ensure the accuracy of its content, outlined in our editorial policy. analysis.event: A new mutation in the influenza A(H1N1) virus, known as G155E, has been identified as a factor in the early start of the flu season. This mutation may be reducing immune recognition and contributing to increased transmission and cases.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Early data shows a significant increase in flu activity, with national test positivity rates rising from 1.3% in early September to nearly 6% in mid-October. Flu hospitalizations have more than doubled since a month ago, reaching over 4,800 cases. There is no evidence so far that people are getting more seriously ill than usual.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The CDC classifies overall flu activity as 'low,' but the early rise in cases and the presence of the G155E mutation are under investigation. Scientists are analyzing the mutation's impact on immune evasion, and experts are monitoring the situation closely.

Flu hospitalizations have more than doubled since a month ago, reaching over 4,800 cases. However, there is no evidence yet that the mutation is causing more severe illness. Experts are monitoring the situation closely, noting that the early surge may be due to immune evasion rather than a 'super flu.' The CDC classifies overall flu activity as 'low,' but the mutation's impact on public health remains under investigation.

news.content_title: Flu Vaccination Linked to Fewer Severe Outcomes in Older Adults, Fewer ED Visits in Children
news.content: Two studies presented at IDWeek 2026 in Washington, DC, add real-world evidence for seasonal influenza vaccination in both older adults and children.1,2 A retrospective cohort study from Geisinger Health System associated vaccination with fewer ICU admissions among older adults who came to the emergency department (ED) with influenza.1 A separate analysis from the CDC’s VISION Network estimated that 2025-2026 seasonal influenza vaccines reduced the risk of influenza-associated ED and urgent care (UC) encounters among children and adolescents by 36%.2 Influenza Vaccination in Older Adults Older adults bear a disproportionate burden of severe influenza, and annual vaccination remains central to prevention.1,3 However, real-world evidence on vaccination and illness severity among ED patients is limited, according to investigators led by presenting author Manouj Kumar, MD. Geisinger serves a mostly rural, older population with substantial comorbidity, which the investigators described as a relevant setting for studying these outcomes.1 The retrospective cohort study included adults aged 65 or older who came to Geisinger EDs with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza between October 1, 2024, and April 30, 2025. Individuals were counted as vaccinated if they had received a seasonal vaccine at least 14 days before presentation, as documented in the electronic health record or immunization registry.1 Lower ICU Admission Rates Among Vaccinated Patients Of 452 patients, 80 (17.7%) were vaccinated. The 2 groups had similar baseline characteristics. Median age was 80 years in vaccinated patients and 78 years in unvaccinated patients. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease was present in 41.3% and 33.9%, respectively.1 ICU admission occurred in 2.5% (2/80) of vaccinated patients compared with 10.5% (39/372) of unvaccinated patients. That is an 8.0-percentage-point absolute difference (P = .029). Vaccinated patients also had shorter stays, although neither difference was significant on two-sided testing:1 The mean hospital stay was 4.43 days versus 5.20 days (P = .091). Among the 41 ICU patients, the mean ICU stay was 0.67 days versus 3.24 days (P = .065). Several outcomes did not differ significantly between groups:1 Hospital admission: 95.0% vs 96.2%; Oxygen use: 75.0% in both groups; Antibiotic prescribing: 47.5% vs 45.2%; and Antiviral prescribing: 90.0% vs 87.4%. The investigators noted that only 17.7% of the cohort had documented vaccination. They said rural access and insurance-related barriers warrant further study. The analyses were unadjusted. Planned next steps include propensity score matching, analyses across multiple seasons, and evaluation of targeted electronic health record vaccination reminders.1 Pediatric Vaccine Effectiveness in the 2025-2026 Season During the 2025-2026 US influenza season, drifted influenza A (H3N2) subclade K viruses predominated, and influenza activity among children was high. To estimate vaccine effectiveness (VE) in this season, investigators led by Katherine Adams, DrPH, MPH, of the CDC’s National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases, used a test-negative design. The study included children and adolescents aged 6 months to 17 years with ED or UC encounters for acute respiratory illness and molecular influenza testing at 6 VISION sites between October 1, 2025, and April 30, 2026. Models were adjusted for age, sex, race and ethnicity, calendar day, and site.2 Of 76,815 encounters, 25,496 were influenza cases and 51,319 were controls. Of the cases, 22% were vaccinated, compared with 29% of controls. Key adjusted VE estimates were as follows:2 Overall: 36% (95% CI, 33%-39%); Influenza A: 38% (95% CI, 35%-41%); Influenza B: 31% (95% CI, 27%-36%); Aged 6 months to 4 years: 47% (95% CI, 42%-51%); Aged 5 to 17 years: 29% (95% CI, 25%-33%); ED encounters: 41% (95% CI, 38%-45%); and UC encounters: 28% (95% CI, 24%-33%). VE was 40% at 14 to 59 days after vaccination, 37% at 60 to 119 days, and 34% at 120 days or more.2 Moderate Effectiveness, Meaningful Impact The VISION investigators concluded that even moderate VE can substantially reduce the influenza burden among children and adolescents. The highest protection was seen in children aged younger than 5. The Geisinger investigators said continued vaccination outreach and adjusted analyses will help translate their findings into clinical practice.1 The VISION authors noted that their findings do not necessarily represent the official position of the CDC.2 REFERENCES 1. Kumar M, Tice AM, Law JM, Kwon T, Wolk DM. Effectiveness of seasonal influenza vaccination in reducing severe outcomes among older adults presenting to the emergency department: a retrospective cohort study. Poster presented at: IDWeek 2026; October 21-October 24; Washington D.C. Submission ID 2416323. 2. Adams K, Reeves EL, Weber ZA, et al. Effectiveness of 2025–2026 seasonal influenza vaccines against US pediatric influenza-associated emergency department and urgent care encounters—VISION Network, October 1, 2025–April 30, 2026. Poster presented at: IDWeek 2026; October 21-October 24; Washington D.C. 3. Grohskopf LA, Ferdinands JM, Blanton LH, et al. Prevention and control of seasonal influenza with vaccines: recommendations of the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices—United States, 2024–25 influenza season. MMWR Recomm Rep. 2024;73(RR-5):1-25. doi:10.15585/mmwr.rr7305a1

analysis.brief_en: Two studies presented at IDWeek 2026 in Washington, DC, provide real-world evidence on the effectiveness of seasonal influenza vaccines. The first study, conducted by Geisinger Health System, found that older adults who received the vaccine had fewer ICU admissions compared to unvaccinated patients. The second study, led by the CDC’s VISION Network, estimated that the 2025-2026 vaccines reduced the risk of influenza-associated emergency department (ED) and urgent care (UC) encounters among children and adolescents by 36%. These findings are based on retrospective cohort and test-negative design analyses, with the latter adjusting for age, sex, race, and other factors. The Geisinger study included adults aged 65 or older with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza between October 1, 2024, and April 30, 2025, while the VISION study covered children and adolescents aged 6 months to 17 years with ED or UC encounters for acute respiratory illness between October 1, 2025, and April 30, 2026. The VISION authors emphasized that even moderate vaccine effectiveness can significantly reduce the influenza burden in children, with the highest protection observed in those under 5 years old. The Geisinger team highlighted the need for further research on barriers to vaccination in rural populations and plans to refine their analyses using propensity score matching.

news.title_zh: 流感 疫苗接种 与老年人的严重后果减少和儿童的急诊就诊次数减少有关 - Pharmacy Times
news.source_body_en: Two studies presented at IDWeek 2026 in Washington, DC, provide real-world evidence on the effectiveness of seasonal influenza vaccines. The first study, conducted by Geisinger Health System, found that older adults who received the vaccine had fewer ICU admissions compared to unvaccinated patients. The second study, led by the CDC’s VISION Network, estimated that the 2025-2026 vaccines reduced the risk of influenza-associated emergency department (ED) and urgent care (UC) encounters among children and adolescents by 36%. These findings are based on retrospective cohort and test-negative design analyses, with the latter adjusting for age, sex, race, and other factors. The Geisinger study included adults aged 65 or older with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza between October 1, 2024, and April 30, 2025, while the VISION study covered children and adolescents aged 6 months to 17 years with ED or UC encounters for acute respiratory illness between October 1, 2025, and April 30, 2026. The VISION authors emphasized that even moderate vaccine effectiveness can significantly reduce the influenza burden in children, with the highest protection observed in those under 5 years old. The Geisinger team highlighted the need for further research on barriers to vaccination in rural populations and plans to refine their analyses using propensity score matching.
news.content_zh: 在华盛顿特区 IDWeek 2026 上发表的两项研究提供了 季节性流感 疫苗 有效性的真实证据。第一项研究由 Geisinger Health System 进行,发现与未接种疫苗的患者相比,接受 疫苗 的老年人入住 ICU 的情况较少。由 CDC VISION Network 领导的第二项研究估计,2025-2026 年 疫苗 将儿童和青少年中与流感相关的急诊室 (ED) 和紧急护理 (UC) 遭遇的风险降低了 36%。这些发现基于回顾性 队列研究 和测试阴性设计分析,后者根据年龄、性别、种族和其他因素进行调整。Geisinger 研究纳入了 2024 年 10 月 1 日至 2025 年 4 月 30 日之间经 RT-PCR 确诊流感的 65 岁或以上成年人,而 VISION 研究涵盖了 2025 年 10 月 1 日至 2026 年 4 月 30 日期间因急性呼吸道疾病而出现 ED 或 UC 的 6 个月至 17 岁的儿童和青少年。VISION 作者强调,即使是中度流感,疫苗 的有效性可显着减轻儿童的流感负担,在 5 岁以下儿童中观察到的保护作用最高。Geisinger 团队强调需要进一步研究农村人口中 疫苗接种 的障碍,并计划使用倾向得分匹配来完善他们的分析。

analysis.brief_en: The article, published on October 25, 2026, discusses the availability and effectiveness of trivalent influenza vaccines in China. It notes that quadrivalent vaccines are no longer available, raising concerns about whether trivalent vaccines are sufficient. According to data from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention, A(H3N2) has become the dominant strain, accounting for 80.6% of all influenza viruses detected, while A(H1N1)pdm09 and B/Victoria account for 19.4% and 33.9%, respectively. The article states that the protection effect of trivalent and quadrivalent vaccines is essentially the same, as the B/Yamagata lineage has not been detected globally since 2020 and has been removed from vaccine components. It also highlights that the flu season typically runs from November to March, and vaccination is recommended now as it takes 2 to 4 weeks for the body to develop protective antibodies. The article does not report any specific case or death counts but emphasizes the importance of vaccination during the current flu season.

analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 文章指出,当前流感季节活跃,建议立即接种疫苗。它还指出,世界卫生组织建议从 疫苗 组件中删除 B/Yamagata 谱系,因为它自 2020 年以来就不再存在。来源是一篇完整的文章,因此没有提及任何限制。

source_language_evidence.time: 2026—2027年度,我国上市的三价流感疫苗包括三价裂解疫苗、三价亚单位疫苗和三价减毒活疫苗。
source_language_evidence.event: 事关流感,中疾控最新发布→ - Sohu。
source_language_evidence.scale_impact_and_risk: 前天09:58 22 一路走好?赵本山灵堂 大衣哥坠楼离世 刘晓庆凌晨去世 谣言个个离谱 娱圈解密 2026.10.16 1.8万 家有这几种人,强烈建议赶紧打流感疫苗→ 洞庭湖边那。
source_language_evidence.brief_en: 顶部 首页 首页 晴 / 14° 隐私 事关流感,中疾控最新发布→ 新浪财经 (来源:新密发布) 新密市各镇卫生院预防接种门诊 💉💉💉 今年接种流感疫苗时 深入探索 搜狐招聘服务 高校招聘会 价值公司联盟 不少人发现四价疫苗不见了 只有三价疫苗 难道是疫苗“降级”了? 据中国疾控中心监测显示,今年7月以来,全国甲型H3N2亚型和乙型Victoria系共同流行,甲型H3N2亚型占比上升,已超过乙型Victoria系。 中国疾控中心发布的流感监测周报进一步反映了这一流行特征: 南、北方省份流感病毒检测阳性率略有上升,全国检出流感阳性样本中甲型流感病毒占比66.1%、乙型流感病毒占比33.9%; 甲型流感病毒中A(H1N1)pdm09占比19.4%、A(H3N2)占比80.6%,乙型流感病毒均为B(Victoria)系。 专家提示,国内的流感高发期通常是11月到次年的3月。接种流感疫苗后,人体需要2到4周才能产生足够的保护性抗体,因此眼下是流感疫苗黄金接种期。 2026—2027年度,我国上市的三价流感疫苗包括三价裂解疫苗、三价亚单位疫苗和三价减毒活疫苗。 其中三价裂解疫苗和亚单位疫苗可以用于6月龄及以上的人群,包括0.25毫升和0.5毫升两种规格。 三价减毒活疫苗适用于3—17岁的人群,每剂次0.2毫升。

supplementary_news.content: 首页 资讯 军事 财经 娱乐 汽车 游戏 文化 援藏 插画 健康 公益 优选 法制 守艺中华 应急中国 更多 佛学文史古诗词人物解梦生活商业成长 地方频道 湖北山东山西丝路 注册登录 中华网 china.com 国内 国际 社会 体育 专题 军事 财经 滚动 三价流感疫苗“够用”吗 应对今年毒株有效 小 大 用微信扫描二维码 分享至好友和朋友圈 关键词: 2026-10-25 11:27:53 央广网·新闻 随着天气转凉,部分地区流感病毒活跃度上升,现在正是接种流感疫苗的最佳时间。然而,今年很多人发现四价疫苗不见了,只剩下三价疫苗,引发了关于疫苗是否“降级”的疑问。 中国疾控中心的监测数据显示,自7月以来,全国甲型H3N2亚型和乙型Victoria系流感病毒共同流行,其中甲型H3N2亚型占比逐渐上升,已超过乙型Victoria系。根据10月22日发布的流感监测周报,南北方省份流感病毒检测阳性率略有上升,全国检出的流感阳性样本中甲型流感病毒占比66.1%,乙型流感病毒占比33.9%。甲型流感病毒中A(H1N1)pdm09占比19.4%,A(H3N2)占比80.6%,乙型流感病毒均为B(Victoria)系。 国内流感高发期通常在11月至次年3月。接种流感疫苗后,人体需要2到4周才能产生足够的保护性抗体,因此目前是接种流感疫苗的最佳时机。 关于三价流感疫苗是否足够应对今年的毒株,专家指出,三价疫苗覆盖了两种甲型流感病毒H1N1和H3N2及乙型流感病毒Victoria系。而四价疫苗在此基础上多覆盖一种乙型流感病毒Yamagata系。由于乙型Yamagata系自2020年3月以来在全球未被监测到,世界卫生组织建议将其从疫苗组分中移除。2026至2027年度,全球流感疫苗将全面调整为三价疫苗。当前情况下,四价疫苗与三价疫苗的保护效果基本一致。 12全文共 2 页下一页 关闭 相关新闻 四价流感疫苗消失了?真相来了 三价疫苗够用吗? 天气转凉,部分地区流感病毒活跃度上升,现在是接种流感疫苗的最佳时间 2026-10-24 11:37:03四价流感疫苗消失了 一线城市房价稳了,三线还能买吗? 在分析2025年房价动向之前,让我们先把焦点回溯至2024年的楼市表现。过去这一年里,房地产市场着实经历了相当大的波动。从年初至年中,无论是一线、二线还是三线城市,新房与二手房市场大多时间都陷入了下滑的困境。然而,时至年末,市场悄然显现出一... 2025-04-03 11:00:32一线城市稳了 三四线城市的房价还能救一下吗? 投资价值不容乐观 一线城市房地产市场有所回暖,企稳目标基本实现;二线城市分化明显:少数强二线城市跟随一线城市的步伐,但大多数二线城市仍在观望;三四线城市则普遍偏冷。当前经济环境下,大部分三四线城市的不动产呈现出一种令人担忧的趋势 2024-12-17 11:38:51三四线城市的房价还能救一下吗 国际金价跌至三周低点 该入局吗 长期持有或有价值 国际金价跌至近三周以来最低点,这是否意味着现在是入手的好时机?Kimi认为短期内金价波动较大,但从长期来看仍有上升动力。黄金价格受地缘政治、购金需求、经济不确定性及通胀预期等多种因素影响,长期持有具备投资价值 2025-08-21 09:06:40国际金价跌至三周低点该入局吗 榴莲价格未来还会跌吗 三重推力揭秘真相 曾经被称为“水果刺客”的榴莲,如今价格大幅下降。自5月以来,全国多地榴莲零售价跌破20元/斤。广州批发市场金枕榴莲最低只要13.8元/斤,北京、上海、武汉等城市的商超里,19.9元/斤的价格牌随处可见 2026-05-10 16:24:17榴莲价格未来还会跌吗 三星S20正式发布!起售价让人止步,你心动了吗 今日凌晨,主题为“TheNextGALAXY”的Samsung Galaxy新品发布会在美国旧金山举行,除了毫无悬念的三星S20正式发布意外,还带来了全新折叠屏方案手机新品。 2020-02-13 09:39:41三星S20正式发布 今日热点 拒让张雪打广告的县委书记为何出圈 克制流量显格局 凯恩获金球奖 颁奖典礼荣耀时刻 全国产算力AI的温度与刻度 让科技温暖人心 甘浙特高压长江大跨越完成架线 西电东送重点工程进展顺利 频道热点 中医小妙招:甲流后“刀片嗓”难受?在家用0成本方法缓解咽痛 广汽埃安陷“香蕉电池”风波 车主诉求更换电池包 环卫工人节致敬“城市美容师” 专属盛会温暖人心 胖东来5名员工遭顾客打骂获补偿 公司坚决维护员工尊严 主编邮箱 网上不良信息举报电话:010-56177181 关于中华网 | 广告服务 | 联系我们 | 招聘信息 | 版权声明 | 豁免条款 | 友情链接 | 中华网动态 版权所有 中华网 今日快讯 浙江调整防台风应急响应为IV级冷空气上线!北方多地迎立秋后最冷一天法国数十万人参与新一轮示威游行 约千人被捕浙江调整防台风应急响应为IV级冷空气上线!北方多地迎立秋后最冷一天法国数十万人参与新一轮示威游行 约千人被捕 ×
